note: SUPPORTING REFERENCE, kept deliberately: a 1940 decorative map that labels the whole 1830s settlement in one view — Fort Dearborn, John Kinzie's House, Ouilmette's Cabin, Miller House, Green Tree Tavern, Mark Beaubien's Sauganash Tavern with 'later site of the Wigwam', Cobweb Castle/Dr. Wolcott, Portier's House, Mackee's House, Burns Cabin, Temple Building, 1st Baptist Church, Tremont House, Chicago Democrat, Eliza Chappell's school, Wm Jones farm, Pottawatomie Village, the street grid, and the trails (Northwest Trail, Green Bay Road, Hubbard's Trace, Whiskey Point Road) plus 'Harbor cut by Engineers 1833'. Its value is orientation and toponym cross-checking, especially for the trail network beyond the platted grid. Its limits are equally clear: it is tier-6 decorative cartography, 105 years after the target date, and demonstrably a composite of different decades on one sheet — it shows Hubbard's Warehouse (1840) and a separate Stage Office alongside 1833 features, both of which this project's date guards exclude from the 1835 scene. Never sole evidence, never traced for geometry.
access_notes: Full sheet legible at the held resolution; a purchased hi-res scan was evaluated 2026-08-09 and declined as adding nothing usable (labels already read cleanly, and more pixels would not change its evidence tier).
